# Pages & Objects {#sec-pages-objects}

This chapter describes the dialogs for pages and for the items on the **Objects** tab.
Along with the options described here, each object's editor includes the shared [**Placement**](#sec-editor-placement) and [**Accessibility**](#sec-editor-accessibility) pages.

## Page {#sec-page-dlg}

The **Page** dialog adds a page to the project or edits the current one.
To open it, click the `r keys("Add")` or `r keys("Edit")` button in the **Pages** section of the **Home** tab.

**Name**: Enter the page's name.

**Layer**: Enter the layer that the page belongs to.
When exporting to SVG, pages can be shown or hidden by layer (see [**Layer controls**](#sec-export-svg)).
Leave this empty for the page to always be visible.

:::: {.optionssection data-latex=""}
::: {.optionssectiontitle data-latex=""}
Position
:::

These options are only shown when adding a page.

**Insert before**: Inserts the new page before the current page.

**Insert after**: Inserts the new page after the current page.
::::

**Rows**: Enter the number of rows in the page's grid.

**Columns**: Enter the number of columns in the page's grid.

The page's grid is shown next to these options.
Drag items from the gallery onto the grid's cells to add them to the page, or select an item in the grid to delete it.
(The **Axis** item requires two or more graphs to already be on the page.)

### Appearance {-}

**Watermark**: Enter the text of a watermark to draw across the page.

**Watermark color**: Select the color of the watermark.

**Background color**: Select the page's background color.

**Background image**: Select an image to draw across the page's background.
Click `r keys("Clear")` to remove it.

**Image opacity**: Enter the opacity of the background image.
A value of 0 is fully transparent, whereas 255 is fully opaque.

**Reset page numbering**: Check this option to restart the page numbering at 1 on this page when printed.

\newpage

## Graphs Section {#sec-graphs-section}

The **Graphs** section of the sidebar is a workspace for creating and exploring graphs.
It is shown below **Analysis** and above the pages.
New graphs are added here by default (see [**Insert into**](#sec-editor-placement)).
When a graph is ready, you can copy it onto a page.

Click a graph in this section to view it.
Each graph is shown by itself and fills the window, rather than being sized like a printed page.
If the graph has a legend, then the legend is shown on the side of the graph chosen in its legend options.

The graph is listed by its title (unless the project file gives it a name).
Graphs without a title are listed as *Graph 1*, *Graph 2*, and so on.
If more than one graph has the same title, then a number is added after it (e.g., *Sales (2)*).

The **Graph** section of the **Graphs** tab works with the graph being shown:

- `r keys("Edit")`: Opens the graph's editor. (You can also double-click the graph.)
- `r keys("Copy to Page")`: Places a copy of the graph on a page (see below).
- `r keys("Delete")`: Removes the graph from this section.
  (You can also select the graph and press `r keys("Delete")`.)

The `r keys("Edit")` and `r keys("Delete")` buttons on the **Objects** tab only work with items on pages.

To place a copy of a graph on a page, view the graph and click `r keys("Copy to Page")`.
Select the page to copy the graph to, and the graph's editor will be shown.
On its [**Placement**](#sec-editor-placement) page, select the cell to place the graph in.
A filtered graph is copied with its filter, and its dataset can't be changed.
The graph stays in the **Graphs** section, so changes to the copy on the page don't affect it.
(You can also select the graph, click `r keys("Copy")`, then select the page and click `r keys("Paste")`.)

::: {.notesection data-latex=""}
Graphs in this section are saved with the project, but they aren't included in exports or when printing all pages.
Filtered graphs in this section aren't linked to filtered graphs on pages.
:::

\newpage

## Label {#sec-label-dlg}

A label is a block of text drawn on a page (e.g., a title or a note).
To insert one, click the `r keys("Label")` button in the **Objects** section of the **Objects** tab.

### Label {-}

**Text**: Enter the label's text.

### Font {-}

**Font**: Select the label's font.

**Font color**: Select the color of the text.

**Include background color**: Check this option to fill the label's background, and select the color.

**Alignment**: Select how the text is aligned (**Left**, **Right**, **Center**, **Justified**, or **Justified (at word)**).

**Line spacing**: Enter the space between the lines of text.

### Appearance {-}

**Orientation**: Select whether the text is drawn **Horizontal** or **Vertical**.

**Visual style**: Select a decorative style for the label's background (e.g., *Index card* or *Lined paper*).
Select **None** to not use a style.

**Box shape**: Select the shape of the label's box.
The word balloon shapes draw the label as a speech balloon, with its tail pointing in the selected direction.

**Box sizing**: Select how the label fits within its cell:

- **Fill the entire area**: The label fills its cell.
- **Shrink height to content**: The label is only as tall as its text.
- **Shrink width to content**: The label is only as wide as its text.
- **Shrink to content**: The label is only as large as its text.

### Header {-}

**Treat first line as header**: Check this option to format the first line of the text as a header.

**Font**, **Color**, and **Alignment**: Select the header's font, color, and alignment.

**Relative scaling**: Enter the size of the header, relative to the rest of the text.

### Shapes {-}

**Left Image**: Select an image to draw to the left of the text.
Click `r keys("Clear")` to remove it.

**Top Image**: Select an image to draw above the text.

**Top Shapes**: Add shapes to draw above the text.

**Top offset (image/shapes)**: Enter the space between the top image (or shapes) and the text.

\newpage

## KPI Card {#sec-kpi-card-dlg}

A KPI (key performance indicator) card shows a single number calculated from a dataset, with optional text beneath it (e.g., *$45.2K* above *Total revenue*).
To insert one, click the `r keys("KPI Card")` button in the **Objects** section of the **Objects** tab.
To edit an existing KPI card, select it and click `r keys("Edit")`.

::: {.tipsection data-latex=""}
To show the number for each value of a column (e.g., each region), click the `r keys("Filtered")` button in the **Graphs** section of the **Graphs** tab and select **KPI Card** as the graph (see [Filtered Graph](#sec-filtered-graph-dlg)).
:::

### Data {-}

**Dataset**: Select the dataset that the number is calculated from.

**Variables**: Click `r keys("Variables...")` to select the **Value** variable.
This is the numeric column whose values are combined into the number.

**Aggregate**: Select how the column's values are combined (**Sum**, **Mean**, **Minimum**, **Maximum**, **Count**, or **Median**).
Missing values are skipped.

**Value**: Shows the number, as it will appear on the card.

### Number {-}

**Font**, **Color**, and **Alignment**: Select the number's font, color, and alignment.
By default, the number is bold and centered.

**Size**: Enter the size of the number, relative to the body text.
The default is 3 (i.e., three times the size of the body text).

### Body {-}

**Text**: Enter the text shown beneath the number (e.g., *Fall Enrollment* or *Less than target*).
This is optional.

::: {.tipsection data-latex=""}
The text can include the project's constants (added from the **Constants** section of the **Data** tab), written in double braces (e.g., `{{Quarter}}`).
These are replaced with the constants' values, so the card updates when the constants change.
:::

**Font**, **Color**, and **Alignment**: Select the body text's font, color, and alignment.
By default, the body text is centered.

### Box {-}

**Preset**: Select the card's style:

- **Standard**: Plain text, with no background.
  The card fills its cell.
- **Index Card**: The text is drawn on an index card, which shrinks to the width of the text.

### Number Format {-}

**Style**: Select how the number is shown:

- **Number**: A number with thousands separators (e.g., *1,204*).
- **Percent**: The number multiplied by 100, followed by a percent sign (e.g., *0.25* is shown as *25%*).
- **Currency**: The number in your system's currency format (e.g., *$45,200*).
- **Number (no thousands separators)**: A number without thousands separators (e.g., *2026*).
- **Accounting**: The same as **Currency**, but negative numbers are shown in parentheses (e.g., *($5,000)*).

**Decimal places**: Enter the number of decimal places to show (0–10).

**Abbreviation**: Select how large numbers are shortened:

- **None**: The full number is shown.
- **Thousands (K)**, **Millions (M)**, or **Billions (B)**: The number is shown in that unit (e.g., *45,200* in thousands is *45K*, or *45.2K* with one decimal place).
- **Automatic**: The largest unit that keeps the number at 1 or more is used.

::: {.notesection data-latex=""}
These units count in thousands.
Some languages count large numbers in ten-thousands instead (e.g., 万 in Chinese and Japanese), so the abbreviations may not suit them.
:::

**Suffix**: Enter text to show after the number (e.g., *pts*).
Include a leading space if you want one between the number and the suffix.

**Missing-value text**: Enter the text shown in place of the number if the column has no values.
The default is a dash (*—*).

**Show plus sign on positive values**: Check this option to show a *+* in front of positive numbers (e.g., *+5%*).

**Preview**: Shows the number with these settings.

## Image {#sec-image-dlg}

An image is a picture file drawn on a page.
To insert an image, click the `r keys("Image")` button in the **Objects** section of the **Objects** tab.

**Image files**: Select the image(s) to insert.
If multiple images are selected, then they are stitched together into one image.

**Stitch direction**: Select whether multiple images are stitched together **Horizontal** or **Vertical**.

### Size {-}

**Override default size**: Check this option to enter the image's size yourself.

**Width** and **Height**: Enter the image's size.

**Resize method**: Select how the image can be resized to fit its cell:

- **Downscale or upscale**: The image can be shrunk or enlarged.
- **Downscale only**: The image can only be shrunk.
- **Upscale only**: The image can only be enlarged.
- **No resize**: The image is drawn at its original size.

### Effect {-}

**Effect**: Select an effect to apply to the image (**None**, **Grayscale**, **Blur horizontal**, **Blur vertical**, **Sepia**, **Frosted glass**, **Oil painting**, or **Color balance**).

\newpage

## Shape {#sec-shape-dlg}

A shape is a predefined icon (e.g., a star or an arrow) drawn on a page.
To insert a shape, click the `r keys("Shape")` button in the **Objects** section of the **Objects** tab.

**Shape**: Select the shape to draw (e.g., *Circle*, *Star*, *Graduation cap*, or *Warning road sign*).

### Size {-}

**Width** and **Height**: Enter the size of the shape.

### Outline {-}

**Color**: Select the color of the shape's outline.

**Style**: Select the outline's style (**Solid**, **Dot**, **Long dash**, **Short dash**, or **Dot dash**).

### Fill {-}

Select the color and pattern to fill the shape with (e.g., **Transparent**, **Cross hatch**, or **Vertical hatch**).

### Label {-}

**Text**: Enter text to draw on the shape.

### Fillable {-}

**Make shape fillable**: Check this option to draw the shape as partially filled.
The lower portion of the shape (its filled percentage) is drawn normally, and the rest is drawn translucent.

**Fill percent**: Enter how much of the shape is filled.

### Repeat {-}

**Count**: Enter the number of times to draw the shape.

### Alignment {-}

**Horizontal**: Select how the shape is aligned horizontally (**Left aligned**, **Centered**, or **Right aligned**).

**Vertical**: Select how the shape is aligned vertically (**Top aligned**, **Centered**, or **Bottom aligned**).

## Common Axis {#sec-common-axis-dlg}

A common axis is a single axis shared by several graphs in the same row (or column) of a page.
To insert one, click the `r keys("Axis")` button in the **Objects** section of the **Objects** tab.
This requires two or more graphs to already be on the page.

When a common axis is created:

- The axis is copied from the tallest graph's left axis (or the widest graph's bottom axis).
- That axis's settings and scale are applied to the other graphs.
- The graphs' own axis labels are turned off, since the common axis serves this purpose.

**Axis type**: Select the type of axis to create (**Bottom X**, **Top X**, **Left Y**, or **Right Y**).

**Connected Graphs**: Check the graphs that the axis is shared with.

**Use common perpendicular axis**: Check this option to also give the graphs the same range on their other axis.
For example, with a common x axis, all the graphs' y axes will use the lowest and highest values across all the graphs.
This is useful for further homogenizing the graphs.

The axis's appearance can be customized on the [**Axis**](#sec-editor-axes) page.

## Spacers & Dividers {#sec-spacers-dividers}

The `r keys("Spacer")` button inserts an empty item, which is useful for adding space between items on a page.

The `r keys("Divider")` button inserts a horizontal or vertical line (single or double) between items.

\newpage

## Filtered Graph {#sec-filtered-graph-dlg}

A filtered graph shows one of a set of graphs, based on a value in a column.
In an exported HTML dashboard, a menu lets the viewer switch between the values.
To insert one, click the `r keys("Filtered")` button in the **Graphs** section of the **Graphs** tab.

**Dataset**: Select the dataset to filter.

**Filter by**: Select the column whose values the graph is filtered by.

**Show by default**: Select the value that is shown in the program and in most exports.

**Graph**: Select the type of graph to create.
Its editor will then be shown to set up the graph.

::: {.notesection data-latex=""}
Filtering only works in exported HTML dashboards.
Filtered graphs that use the same dataset and column are linked together.
The value chosen here will also be shown on the other linked graphs, including those on other pages.
:::

To change the value shown on a filtered graph in the program, select the graph and click the `r keys("Filter")` button in the **Sources** section of the **Data** tab.
